# Provider accounts, logout and tenant isolation

- Entry ID: ports-and-adapters/provider-account-security
- Researched: 4–5 November 2026; version 1.0.
- Status: implemented and verified with local unit/PostgreSQL checks; live identity/operational checks remain outstanding.
- Question: adapt the explicitly authorised Salesync account/logout/tenant structure to CEREMO without inheriting its ownership and logout limitations.
- Approved requirement: one provider business is one tenant, with an accountable owner and invited team. Customers retain independent accounts. A workspace's ACTIVE status grants no listing approval, trial, subscription, verification badge or rating.
- Scope: Java 25, Boot 4.1.1, Spring Security 7.1.1, Hibernate/JPA and PostgreSQL 18.0. Production PostgreSQL version remains unselected. No remote service, skill installation or live realm reset was authorised or performed.

Actual deployed realm claims still require testing. |

The existing CEREMO identity adapter now accepts that known framework type using exact external-form comparison; it still rejects arbitrary objects and foreign issuers. | Browser and API claim conversion differ. A synthetic String issuer alone did not cover this compatibility case. Apache-2.0. |

No request Origin or arbitrary return URL is used. | Apache-2.0; API usage, not copied class code. No post-logout return URI is selected. The full Next.js session strategy remains open. |

API logout blocks this session in CEREMO; the client still performs standard IdP logout to end SSO. | No admin API credentials or non-standard refresh-token logout call are introduced. IdP back-channel logout ingestion remains future work. |

Test two tenants and revoked access. | Guidance informs the design; it does not certify it or establish Ghanaian demand. |
| [PostgreSQL 18 transaction isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/transaction-iso.html#XACT-READ-COMMITTED) | Acquire the root lock before a fresh membership query. At READ COMMITTED, later statements observe newly committed revocations. | A query's pre-lock snapshot is insufficient. The implementation depends on READ COMMITTED; do not silently change isolation or use stale feature caches. |

Useful primary sources were sufficient for this implementation. No inaccessible Slack/LinkedIn posts or unattributed Medium advice were used as evidence. No popularity counts or engineer credentials are claimed.

## Implementation and reuse

The existing `usermanagement` module remains the source of account registration, activation, identity mapping and persistence. The new `account` module adds `Accounts.currentAccount`, `requireActiveAccount` and `requireAdministrator`. Its HTTP projection reuses `RestUserResponse`; it never exposes JWT claims, credentials or arbitrary roles. `UserDirectory` is an internal existence port implemented inside User Management, not a public search endpoint.

The new `tenant` module stores the owner on the root. Team invitations allow MANAGER/FINANCE only; the owner cannot be removed or replaced through these operations. Invitations target an already registered CEREMO UUID supplied privately by the recipient. Only the current invitee can accept. There is no public customer/email lookup. Invitations have no automated email delivery or invented expiry policy in this increment. Future UI work must provide a safe invitation handoff.

Every tenant application operation checks the caller through `Accounts`. Team management requires the root owner. Administrative suspension/reactivation additionally requires ROLE_ADMIN, trusted `amr` containing `mfa`, and a Long epoch-second `auth_time` no more than five minutes old and not in the future. These are fail-closed technical requirements; the live Keycloak flow must actually establish MFA and emit those claims. A hardcoded user attribute named amr is not acceptable. The development pre-verified admin fixture is not proof of assurance.

Suspended workspaces remain readable to their members; owners may inspect the team and revoke access. New invitations and acceptance are blocked. The existing public marketplace is still planned. Future listing/enquiry/billing use cases must check tenant status and the specific member role as well as their own entitlement/ownership rules. `TenantAccounts.get()` alone is not permission to edit any provider feature.

`TransactionalTenantAccounts` provides the outer Spring transaction; repository methods require it. Point operations lock the root, then read membership in a separate statement. Mutation and `tenant_audit` append commit together. Unauthorised/missing businesses return the same 404. Listings and team lists reuse bounded `CeremoPageable`/`RestCeremoPageable`, not unrestricted collection reads. Database FKs, unique membership and status/role checks supplement application rules.

The new `logout` core receives the trusted current session through an outbound port. PostgreSQL stores issuer, session ID, subject and revocation time, never raw access/refresh/ID tokens. Unique issuer/session plus ON CONFLICT makes repeat storage safe. JWT decoding validates signatures/claims before checking revocation, without a revocation cache. A storage failure denies authentication with a safe message. Revocations are retained without automatic expiry so a refresh cannot resurrect a revoked session; retention/cleanup must be designed against the actual IdP session lifetime before production scale.

POST `/api/v1/logout` returns 204 after commit; further bearer requests for that session return 401. Already in-flight operations are not cancelled. The frontend must clear its tokens and complete standard IdP logout. CSRF-protected browser POST `/logout` records the browser session revocation, clears local authentication and uses Spring's registered-provider OIDC redirect. No return URL is taken from a request header. Neither path promises that all other sessions or other applications have logged out.

Shared reuse: `Assert`, `CeremoException`, existing advice/message sources, `CeremoUUID`, `TenantId`, `TenantSuspendedException`, `BaseEntity`, pagination, `AuthenticatedUser` and `SpringCurrentUser`. Wire reuse: existing Clock, CORS, separate bearer/browser chains, database scanning/auditing, UserAccounts transaction boundary and OpenAPI beans. The optional inherited JWT-organisation tenant filter/aspects remain disabled; they are not the membership authority for the new tenant module. No Lombok or new runtime dependency was added.

Additive migrations: `V202611040001__create_session_revocations.sql` and `V202611040002__create_provider_tenants.sql`. The original account migration is untouched. A future provider profile must reference one tenant uniquely; the provider/profile/subscription tables remain planned. Tenant creation does not trigger a trial.

## Configuration and remaining work

Removed the unused keycloak.admin block, including its embedded credential, from application YAML. The new-import development realm enables email verification, brute-force protection, refresh rotation with zero reuse, login/admin event recording and a twelve-hour maximum session. Its unused admin client/service account is disabled. This changes the import fixture only. Existing realms/volumes were not reset, updated or queried with administrative credentials. Previously deployed credentials need review and rotation by their operator; source removal does not revoke them or erase history.

Before public use: prove real SMTP/verification/refresh, configure and test staff MFA/auth_time/amr, review roles and service accounts, apply approved current-realm changes, select production database version, add distributed request/resource limits, test dependency/key rotation and incident/recovery procedures, select Next.js session/logout integration and complete required Sonar/operational gates. Timestamp auditing remains separate from the new tenant-specific event history; no general AuditorAware implementation is claimed. Recovery, account restriction administration, ownership transfer, subscription billing and provider publication remain separate features.

## Verification

Unit checks cover caller/status/staff policy, strict access-token claims, revocation failures, session mapping and plain application rules. The integration suite uses disposable PostgreSQL 18.0 plus a loopback OIDC discovery/JWKS fixture and real RSA-signed JWTs through the production decoder. It tests account/tenant HTTP, separate businesses, invitation consent/revocation, staff gates, logout, rollback and a lock/revocation race. This is stronger than mocked principal tests but is not a live Keycloak/SMTP/MFA test.

Final build, coverage counters and remaining tooling limitations are recorded in the [quality register](../quality/tests-and-analysis.md). Grammarly: version 1.0, local prose reviewed 5 November 2026; external check unavailable/pending. No company text was uploaded and no score or human-authorship certification is claimed.

Final run, 5 November: `.\gradlew.bat check bootJar --console=plain` passed; 525 unit + 48 PostgreSQL cases, zero failures/errors/skips. Combined JaCoCo reports 2141/2141 lines and 443/443 branches, with zero missed counters per class. See the [exact quality record](../quality/tests-and-analysis.md#provider-account-security-5-november-2026). ## Account module consolidation, 5 November 2026

- Approval: the founder accepted consolidating usermanagement and account into one account module. This supersedes the four-package arrangement described earlier in this entry; the identity, tenant and logout policies remain unchanged.
- Question: remove the unnecessary feature split without changing local account records, HTTP contracts or the trusted identity/transaction boundary.
- Status: implementation and clean full-build verification complete; see the [current quality record](../quality/tests-and-analysis.md#account-consolidation-5-november-2026).

### Evidence and design choice

Reviewed [Spring Modulith fundamentals](https://docs.spring.io/spring-modulith/reference/fundamentals.html), manual 2.1.1, on 5 November. It describes modules as units of functionality with provided interfaces and private implementation, and supports starting with a simple arrangement. CEREMO chooses one cohesive account feature; the manual does not prescribe our package name or require a service class per module. Spring Modulith was not added as a dependency.

Reviewed [Spring TransactionTemplate v7.0.9](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/v7.0.9/spring-tx/src/main/java/org/springframework/transaction/support/TransactionTemplate.java), execute and rollback handling, Apache-2.0. The existing decorator already protects complete lifecycle operations. Keep that boundary while moving packages; a configuration merge is not permission to call the repository without it. No reference source was copied.

Spring Petclinic's [OwnerController](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-petclinic/blob/main/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerController.java) and [OwnerRepository](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-petclinic/blob/main/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerRepository.java), reviewed from actual raw source, illustrate related components in one owner feature. Its controller/repository dependency is not adopted: CEREMO retains inbound ports and a plain core. Main is an evolving learning sample, not version-pinned production evidence or proof of our architecture. The GitHub directory UI initially returned a loading error; raw files were used instead. No code or dependency was imported, and no author credentials or star counts are claimed.

### Current implementation

All former usermanagement production/unit/PostgreSQL files now live beneath account. The domain remains User/UserIdentity/UserStatus, with UserRepository in domain/repository. UserService retains registration and activation; AccountService retains current-account, active-account and staff checks inside the same feature. They are focused collaborators, not separate modules or login systems. UserAccounts/CurrentUser/UserDirectory and DTOs/JPA/security/transaction adapters moved with the feature.

One wire/account/AccountConfiguration now composes Clock, UserRepository, UserDirectory, transactional UserAccounts, StaffAccess and Accounts. UserRegistrationProperties moved beside it without changing its prefix, bounds or terms policy. The duplicate configuration was removed; wire now has 16 Java files in nine areas. Tenant/logout/shared-security imports and test fixtures use account. AccountConfigurationTest verifies a single lifecycle bean plus the account/staff ports. AccountArchitectureTest retains framework/HTTP boundaries and rejects any production usermanagement package.

Shared UUIDs, assertions, errors, identity helpers, BaseEntity, paging and central security/CORS/database wiring are reused. No new helper, runtime dependency, migration or compatibility alias was introduced. Existing /api/v1/users/me, /api/v1/account, activation, tenant and logout routes are preserved; PostgreSQL table names, constraints and rows are unchanged. Old package names in dated research/test commands describe history; use current source and ADR 11.9 for new work. Relative links were redirected to moved files rather than leaving broken paths.

Focused command: `.\gradlew.bat test --tests '*AccountConfigurationTest' --tests '*AccountArchitectureTest' --tests '*AccountServiceTest' --tests '*UserServiceTest' --tests '*UserActivationServiceTest' --console=plain` passed. Final `.\gradlew.bat clean check bootJar --console=plain` passed: 525 regular and 48 PostgreSQL tests, zero failures/errors/skips; 2139 lines and 443 branches covered, none missed per class. The packaged JAR contains no legacy usermanagement classes. Exact counters and limitations are in [the quality register](../quality/tests-and-analysis.md#account-consolidation-5-november-2026). No existing realm, business database, customer record or live external service was changed. Sonar and live identity checks remain separate.
